question: Xi Jinping out before 2027?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if China's General Secretary of the Communist Party, Xi Jinping, is removed from power for any length of time between July 3, 2025, and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

CCP General Secretary Xi Jinping will be considered removed from power if he announces his resignation from his role as General Secretary, or is otherwise dismissed, detained, disqualified, or otherwise loses his position or is prevented from fulfilling his duties as General Secretary within this market's timeframe.

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

eventMetadata.context_description: Xi Jinping's entrenched authority within the Chinese Communist Party, reinforced by years of institutional consolidation and military purges, underpins the 95.5% trader consensus that he will remain in his roles as general secretary and president through the end of 2026. With the 21st Party Congress scheduled for 2027 likely to formalize a fourth term, no designated successor has emerged, and recent public activities—including economic planning sessions and diplomatic engagements—show no signs of weakening control or internal challenges. Speculation around health or elite discontent from prior periods has not produced verifiable shifts. Low-probability disruptions, such as an unforeseen medical event or abrupt leadership transition outside normal congress timelines, remain the primary factors that could still alter this trajectory before the resolution date.
